questions.q: Why does the lesson say that an AI agent's decisions should not all execute automatically?
options: Because Power Automate technically cannot run AI-triggered actions
Because the cost of a wrong decision isn't the same for every action — high-stakes or irreversible actions deserve human review before they execute
Because Copilot Studio agents are never confident enough to be trusted
Because approvals are required by law for all cloud flows
questions.explain: A wrong tool call on a low-risk lookup is harmless, but a wrong call on something like a refund or an auto-close has real, sometimes irreversible consequences — which is why those specific actions warrant a human checkpoint.

questions.q: Which Power Automate approval action is almost always the right choice for a human-in-the-loop gate that should stop the flow until a person responds?
options: Create an approval
Wait for an approval
Start and wait for an approval
Respond to the agent
questions.explain: Start and wait for an approval creates the approval request and pauses the flow at that step until an approver responds, which is exactly the behavior a human-in-the-loop gate needs.

questions.q: Which approval type requires every assigned approver to respond before the flow continues?
options: Approve/Reject — First to respond
Approve/Reject — Everyone must approve
Custom Responses — Wait for one response
Sequential approval only applies to first responses
questions.explain: "Everyone must approve" requires a response from every assigned approver before the flow proceeds (or stops immediately on a rejection) — the strictest of the approval types for all-respond scenarios.

questions.q: Why can't a Start and wait for an approval step simply live inside the same flow that a Copilot Studio agent calls directly as a tool?
options: Because approvals are not supported in agent flows at all
Because a flow called by an agent must respond synchronously within roughly 100 seconds, and a human approval can take minutes or hours
Because Copilot Studio only allows one action per flow
Because approvals require a different Microsoft 365 license than agent flows
questions.explain: An agent-connected tool flow must respond within the 100-second limit. A human approval can't realistically happen that fast, so the approval step needs to live in a separate flow that isn't the one the agent is synchronously waiting on.

questions.q: What is the practical two-flow pattern described in this lesson for gating an AI-proposed action?
options: One flow does everything, including the approval, inside the 100-second window
A first flow does fast, synchronous work and responds to the agent right away; a second, separately triggered flow runs the approval with no time limit
Two identical flows run in parallel for redundancy
The first flow handles the approval, and the second flow is only used for logging
questions.explain: The flow the agent calls directly handles only the fast, synchronous work and responds quickly. A separate flow, triggered independently, runs the slower approval step without the 100-second constraint.
